title: Sensex Snaps Two-Day Losing Streak on IT Surge but Posts Third Straight Weekly Loss
excerpt: IT stocks rally 3.5% on Nvidia earnings boost while new closing auction mechanism and Fed speech jitters weigh on weekly performance
body:
• The Sensex gained 331 points (0.43%) to close at 77,264.51, while the Nifty rose 85 points (0.35%) to 24,175.65, snapping a two-day losing run on Friday.
  • The Nifty IT index surged 3.5%, led by TCS, Tech Mahindra, and Infosys, after strong quarterly results from U.S. chipmaker Nvidia boosted global tech sentiment.
  • Despite Friday's gains, both benchmarks posted a third consecutive weekly loss — the longest falling streak in five months — weighed by concerns over SEBI's new closing auction mechanism and caution ahead of the Fed Chair's speech.

Indian equity benchmarks ended higher on Friday, snapping a two-day losing streak as a broad rally in information technology stocks offset lingering concerns about the new closing auction mechanism and the Federal Reserve's interest rate outlook.

The BSE Sensex climbed 330.92 points, or 0.43%, to settle at 77,264.51, while the NSE Nifty 50 added 84.80 points, or 0.35%, to close at 24,175.65. The Indian rupee also found support, ending 0.2% higher at 95.38 against the U.S. dollar.

IT Stocks Lead the Charge

The Nifty IT index was the standout performer, surging 3.5% on the back of upbeat quarterly results from U.S. chipmaker Nvidia, which lifted global technology sentiment. Tech Mahindra led the charge with a 4% gain, followed by Tata Consultancy Services, Infosys, HCL Technologies, and Wipro.

Wipro added an extra 2% after announcing a partnership with Google Cloud, while Tejas Networks advanced 7% following a letter of intent from TCS.

Beyond tech, metal and pharma stocks also contributed to the rally, with both sectoral indices gaining 0.4%. More than 160 stocks touched 52-week highs, including Redington, Oracle Financial Services, Bajaj Auto, Divis Labs, and Solar Industries.

Weekly Pain Persists

Despite Friday's recovery, both benchmarks posted their third consecutive weekly decline — the longest falling streak in five months. For the week, the Nifty fell 0.3% and the Sensex lost 0.4%, with 10 of 16 major sectors ending in the red.

The broader market showed resilience, with the Nifty MidCap and SmallCap indices each gaining about 0.5% for the week, supported by earnings-driven buying and sustained domestic fund inflows.

Closing Auction Draws Scrutiny

India's new closing auction session, which determines official closing prices for futures and options-eligible stocks, remained a focal point after sharp moves on recent derivatives expiry days. On Tuesday, the Nifty's indicative price swung from negative 0.24% to negative 1.4%, and on Thursday's monthly expiry, BSE derivatives turnover hit an 11-month low as the indicative close briefly dropped more than 3%.

SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said Thursday that the regulator was not considering immediate changes to the mechanism despite the market swings.

"The key market concern is whether the closing auction can absorb large institutional orders without creating excessive price dislocation or liquidity stress."

— Niharika Tripathi, Head of Products and Research, Wealthy.in

The MSCI rebalancing effective after markets close on August 31 will offer a key test, as passive-fund flows could lead to substantial order concentration during the auction window.

Key Movers

Among major stocks, HDFC Bank slipped 0.9% for the week after a U.S. class-action lawsuit alleged illegal payments. The lender called the suit "without merit" and said it intends to vigorously defend itself. Reliance Industries lost 2.2%, while Bharti Airtel fell 3.3% after major shareholder Singtel signaled plans to adjust its stake.

On the positive side, Just Dial surged 10% after Kotak Institutional Equities retained a 'Buy' rating with a target price of Rs 1,175.

Looking Ahead

Markets enter the coming week with the MSCI rebalancing as the immediate catalyst, while traders remain watchful of crude oil prices, which have been pressuring margins, and the Federal Reserve's rate trajectory. The Sensex and Nifty continue to trade below their 50-day moving averages, signaling a cautious technical outlook despite Friday's bounce.
nri_angle: Indian stock market performance directly affects NRI portfolios and mutual fund investments, with the IT sector rally particularly relevant given the large Indian tech diaspora.
